item.title: What to Do in N.Y.C. This Winter
item.description: The shows to see, hear, and watch in TV, art, contemporary music, theatre, movies, classical music, and dance.

item.title: Corruption on the Ballot
item.description: Corruption is always an issue, but this year will it finally catapult from a topic of chronic bellyaching to an actual mechanism for changing votes?
item.dc:creator: ByRuth Marcus

item.title: The Party Girls at the Heart of “Club Kid”
item.description: Jordan Firstman’s directorial début tells the story of a gay promoter who finds out he’s a father. On a groggy Lower East Side morning, the three actors who play his night-life posse compare notes on queer family planning.
item.dc:creator: ByHolden Seidlitz

item.title: Reliving the Bronx’s Biggest Battle
item.description: In 1776, Continental Army soldiers defended what is now Glover’s Rock from the British. The other day, reënactors did it all again at Orchard Beach.
item.dc:creator: ByIan Frazier

item.title: Dante de Blasio Is Off Vocal Rest
item.description: As a newborn, the son of the former mayor won free music lessons for life at the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music—and then he quit. Now he’s finding his way back to the notes.
item.dc:creator: ByJane Bua

item.title: New Jersey, the Diesel State
item.description: A data center in the Meadowlands recently leaked five thousand gallons of fuel into a nearby creek. The Riverkeeper of the Hackensack gives a tour.
item.dc:creator: ByRobert Sullivan

item.title: An Exiled Filmmaker’s Unsparing View of Contemporary Russia
item.description: Andrey Zvyagintsev’s “Minotaur” is the first independent feature to portray Russian life during the war with Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: ByJoshua Yaffa

item.title: Why Immigration Agents Don’t Quit in Protest
item.description: How a culture of dehumanization and denial keepsICEand Border Patrol personnel “at war with an enemy that does not fight back.”
item.dc:creator: ByFrancisco Cantú

item.title: The Year Math Changed Forever
item.description: A.I. is solving problems that stumped the field for decades. Mathematicians look to Terence Tao for guidance on their altered world.
item.dc:creator: ByRivka Galchen

item.title: Did the World Just Gain Hundreds of Millions of Alzheimer’s Patients?
item.description: A new definition of Alzheimer’s includes people without symptoms. Experts are fiercely divided over whether that makes sense—and whether the new drugs really help.
item.dc:creator: ByManvir Singh

item.title: Common Scams to Avoid
item.description: Thinking of throwing that ball for your dog? He might be scamming you.
item.dc:creator: ByJack Handey

item.title: “Family Lore”
item.description: Fatal, the internet kept saying. Once symptoms began, the disease was almost always fatal.
item.dc:creator: ByTéa Obreht

item.title: The Telephone’s Tangled History of Intimacy and Control
item.description: How an invention that brought distant voices close rewrote the rules of conversation and raised an unsettling question: Who else might be listening?
item.dc:creator: ByCal Revely-Calder

item.title: Briefly Noted
item.description: “Music Against the Night,” “Her Kind,” “A World We Share,” and “The Flying Death.”

item.title: The Trouble with Saying What You Mean
item.description: In “The Channel,” the poet Jana Prikryl borrows voices from Shakespeare and her own past to explore exile, family, and the possibilities of expressing private grief.
item.dc:creator: ByLangdon Hammer

item.title: Roy Lichtenstein’s Witty Critiques of Masculinity
item.description: The artist’s best work, in a new retrospective at the Whitney Museum, directs his campy humor at gender stereotypes.
item.dc:creator: ByHilton Als

item.title: A Song of Grief and Union in “Lincoln in the Bardo”
item.description: Missy Mazzoli’s operatic adaptation of George Saunders’s novel is a charismatic, openhearted work.
item.dc:creator: ByNathan Heller

item.title: “Wild Horse Nine” Gets Lost on Easter Island
item.description: Martin McDonagh’s comic thriller, set on the eve of the Pinochet dictatorship, diverts our tears toward the mortality of a cancer-riddled C.I.A. agent.
item.dc:creator: ByJustin Chang

item.title: “I Love You in the Morning”
item.description: “What makes up a life?”
item.dc:creator: ByEllen Bass

item.title: “Form and Function”
item.description: “I tried, but I was too small to lift you / Up and out of that bathtub—”
item.dc:creator: ByPaul Tran
